finding: S1A colour scale is z-scored, not DSB units
evidence: Scripts/3. Manuscript/Figure_1.R line 1012 calls DotPlot() with default scale=TRUE, col.min=-2.5, col.max=2.5. DotPlot z-scores each feature across groups and clips to +/-2.5 SD.
answers_reviewer: YES — this is the whole explanation for the -1 to 2 range. The panel never showed DSB values.
action: State in the S1A legend and Methods that the colour scale is the z-scored group mean (Seurat DotPlot default), not DSB-normalised protein units.

finding: Isotype subtraction is NOT the cause
evidence: DSBNormalizeProtein was called with denoise.counts=TRUE and use.isotype.control=TRUE over 7 isotypes (Mouse-IgG1/2a/2b, Rat-IgG1/2a/2b, Hamster-IgG) — the recommended configuration. The isotypes themselves have median 0.000 and q99 0.000, i.e. correctly centred on background, while real markers reach q99 11.14 and max 53.05.
answers_reviewer: NO — the user's hypothesis is not supported. Isotype-based denoising removes a per-cell technical component; it does not compress the dynamic range of real markers, and the isotypes sitting at zero is evidence it worked.
action: Say the isotype controls behaved as intended and give their distribution.

finding: The data DO reach the reviewer's expected range
evidence: CD8A q99 30.35 (max 46.98); CD19 q99 16.96; CD3D q99 11.91; CD27 q99 11.56. Within positive populations: CD8A median 16.70 in CD8 T cells, CD19 median 6.99 in B cells, CD3D median 4.85 in CD4 T cells. 61 of 137 markers have q99 > 5, 29 > 10, 4 > 20.
answers_reviewer: YES — refutes the premise directly. The reviewer expected 5-20 and the data delivers that; only the FIGURE'S SCALE was misleading.
action: Quote these numbers in the response and add a supplementary panel showing raw DSB distributions for lineage markers.

finding: Negative DSB values were lost to sparse coercion — disclose
evidence: Scripts/1. QC/1.DSB_Norm.R line 260 does Matrix(as.matrix(cells.dsb.norm), sparse=TRUE). DSB legitimately returns negatives for below-background markers, but a dgCMatrix stores them as structural zeros: the stored ADT data layer has min 0, no negative values, and 81.7% exact zeros.
answers_reviewer: PARTLY — not what the reviewer asked, but it is a real consequence of the pipeline that a careful reader could find, and it affects the LOW end of the scale they commented on.
action: Disclose in Methods: negative DSB values (below-background) are truncated to zero by sparse storage. This does not affect positive-population calls or any ADT gate used (all thresholds are positive), but it means the stored floor is 0 rather than the negative values DSB emits.
